title: Incudo game system definition
description: The contract behind ADR 0011's promise: if a system definition validates against this schema, the app can build characters in it. This file is a public API — see ADR 0011 for the versioning policy. Validation here is STRUCTURAL, not semantic: a system can be valid and still be a poor model of its game, which is the author's business. What validating guarantees is that the app will not crash and will not silently misread the file.

formatVersion.description: The version of this format, not of the system. Bumped only by a breaking change to the format itself.

id.patternDescription: must be lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, e.g. "dnd5e" or "my-house-rules"

version.description: The system definition's own version. Overlays record the parent version they were written against.

extends.description: The id of an official system this one overlays. ADR 0011.

elementTypes.description: The type vocabulary content may use — the list Aurora hardcodes.

stats.description: Stats shared by every character kind. A kind may add its own, or replace one by name.

generationMethods.description: How a build step's budget can produce its starting values (ADR 0017). Declared once for the system and referenced by id from a step's budget, because a PC and an NPC generate ability scores the same way and the cost table should not be written twice.

characterKinds.description: At least one. A system with no kinds can build nothing. ADR 0009.

auroraTypeMap.description: Aurora element types that map onto this system's types. Only needed to consume Aurora content.

licence.description: ADR 0010. Required on official systems; the app does not enforce it on user systems.

bound.description: A stat bound: a plain number, or an expression over stats. Applied to every stat — contributed, derived or both — after contributions and derivations settle and before overrides, which still win (ADR 0016). An expression is what the interesting bounds need: 5e's ability score maximum is `20 + strength:max`, because the corpus keeps only the delta and Aurora hardcodes the 20. Bounds read the unclamped values of other stats, in one pass.

expr.description: A stat expression. Deliberately not a scripting language: no loops, no I/O, and a fixed function set. Content comes from the internet.

oneOf.description: A number read out of a declared row, indexed by another expression (ADR 0018). For the published numbers that are a table and have no closed form: 5e's multiclass spell slots are twenty rows of nine. The index is floored and clamped to the array, so a value below the row reads its first entry and one above reads its last.

progression.description: How a kind of character advances. ADR 0009.

stat.description: The stat the level is published as. Defaults to "level", which is what levelled content references.

elementIdPattern.description: An element id granted once per step of progression, with "{n}" replaced by the step number: "ID_LEVEL_{n}" gives a level 8 character ID_LEVEL_1 through ID_LEVEL_8. Aurora writes exactly those into every save and its content references them; without this, a character built in Incudo cannot match one built in Aurora. Only whole-numbered steps are granted.

trackStatPattern.description: The stat each track publishes its own count as, with "{name}" replaced by the track element name, lowercased: "level:{name}" on a character whose levels went to the Warlock element gives level:warlock = 18. A track is an element the character spent progression on (ADR 0015); grants inherit their granter’s track, so a class feature's level gate reads its own class's level rather than the character's total. 150-odd references in the Aurora corpus read these stats and nothing in the corpus writes them — Aurora computes them in application code. Omit it and no track stats are published.

characterKind.description: Only `id` is required, because a kind may `extends` another and state just its differences. A kind that extends nothing needs progression, elementTypes, buildSteps and sheet to be buildable — the app reports a kind missing those as unusable rather than refusing to load the system.

id.patternDescription: must be lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, e.g. "pc" or "legendary"

extends.description: The id of another kind in this system. "legendary" is a delta on "npc", not a copy of it.

elementTypes.description: When the kind extends another, an entry may be written "+Type" to add or "-Type" to remove; a list with no prefixed entry replaces the parent's outright.

grants.description: Element ids every character of this kind has without choosing them. The system-definition home for what Aurora answers in application code: a 5e character has a base armour class and adds its Constitution modifier to hit points, and no content file says so. Not stored on the character, so fixing the baseline fixes every character rather than only the ones saved afterwards.

trackStat.description: A stat contributed once per track (ADR 0018). ADR 0015 gave every track a published count that content reads by name; this is the part that iterates — "for each track, add half its count" — which a system definition cannot write out, because content ships its own tracks. For every track the character has, if `when`'s element is in that track, `value` is evaluated and added to `stat`. Track contributions land with content's, before derivations read them.

stat.description: The stat contributed to. `{name}` is replaced with the track element's lowercased name, which turns an aggregate into a per-track stat: "{name}:spellcasting:solo" publishes warlock:spellcasting:solo. Without it, every track's contribution sums into one stat.

when.description: Only contribute for tracks containing this element. Omit to contribute for every track. This is the hook content already provides: a 5e casting class grants a marker saying which weighting it uses, and the marker lands in that class's track.

value.description: Evaluated once per matching track. The reserved reference "track:progress" reads that track's own count.

types.description: May be empty: a step can be about entering numbers rather than picking elements.

requires.description: Ids of steps that must be usable before this one is (ADR 0017). A genuine dependency and nothing else — you cannot pick spells before something makes you a spellcaster. The suggested order is a topological sort of these with the declared array order breaking ties, so a step that requires nothing sorts first; a step whose dependencies are unmet is not yet available rather than skippable.

budget.description: A pool of points a build step distributes (ADR 0017). `stat` is an ordinary stat, so content adds to it with the `stat` rule that already exists — a feat, a race variant, an improvement at level 4 — and the step reopens on its own when it does. That is the answer to "a class gave you one more attribute point and you should not have to walk back to an earlier screen".

methods.description: Ids of the system's generationMethods this step offers.

generationMethod.description: How a budget's starting values are produced (ADR 0017). Data rather than code, because docs/CODE-REUSE-POLICY.md rule 1 says a rule about the game may not live in a component, and a point-buy cost table is exactly that. Three shapes: `pool` plus `costs` is a points method; `values`, or `dice` with `count`, hands out a set to assign; neither means the user types numbers.

dice.description: Dice notation the shell rolls, e.g. "4d6dl1". Core never rolls anything.
